description:
Tebra only initiates contact with candidates via email from an official Tebra email address (@tebra.com, @patientpop.com, or @kareo.com) or through our applicant tracking system, Greenhouse.Â We will only ask you to provide sensitive personal information through our official application portal â not via social media or text message. We do not conduct interviews via instant messaging.

About the Role

Tebra helps private practices bring modernized care to patients everywhere. To run our own business well, every team needs numbers it can trust.

We're looking for a Senior Analytics Engineer to help build Tebra's new internal analytics platform. You'll turn data from Salesforce, NetSuite, Stripe, our product, and other systems into one shared, tested set of business data and metrics that Finance, Customer Success, Growth, and Payments all use. You'll lead projects end to end, set the standards others build on, and partner with business leaders to define the metrics that matter most.

Your Area of Focus

  • Â Data Modeling & Shared Datasets: Design, build, and maintain enterprise-wide business data that teams across Finance, Customer Success, Growth, and Payments build on. Apply dimensional modeling and layered design (staging, intermediate, and marts) so business logic lives in one place and isn't rebuilt by each team.
  • Metric Definition & Semantic Layer: Partner with metric owners in Finance and the business to define each key metric once, with a named owner and documented logic. Publish governed metrics in a semantic layer that Tableau, AI assistants, and other tools query, and reconcile them to current reporting and the general ledger before teams switch over.
  • Self-Service Enablement: Build easy-to-use datasets that let non-technical teammates and analysts answer their own questions without writing complex joins.
  • Platform Migration: Lead projects end to end on the new internal analytics platform, from source data to dashboards. Move each team's reporting over one domain at a time, with clear cutover and rollback plans, and onboard the analysts who contribute to new conventions, review processes, and tools.
  • Data Quality & Testing: Build automated tests and pull-request checks so data issues are caught before they reach reports. Monitor scheduled jobs, fix failures, and recover runs as part of shared production support.
  • Performance & Efficiency: Tune SQL, models, and pipeline schedules so data refreshes on time and dashboards load in seconds. Monitor compute usage and cost, and choose how each model is built and refreshed to keep both in check.
  • Forecasting & Machine Learning: Partner with analysts and data scientists to prepare clean, documented datasets for forecasting and machine learning models, such as retention and revenue projections.
  • Code Review & Mentorship: Review code from analysts and engineers across teams, and coach them on modeling, SQL, and testing standards.
  • Governance & Documentation: Follow data-sharing and privacy rules that keep protected health information (PHI) and personal data out of internal analytics. Maintain model documentation, lineage, and metric definitions via dbt, GitHub, Confluence, and Jira.

Your Professional Qualifications

  • Experience: 5+ years of experience in analytics engineering, data engineering, or a similar role, with 2+ years hands-on in dbt in production.
  • SQL Fluency: Expert SQL, including window functions, CTEs, and performance tuning for queries and pipelines on large datasets.
  • Data Modeling: Deep proficiency in dimensional modeling (Kimball), including shared datasets that serve many teams.
  • Tech Stack: Proven experience with Snowflake or a similar cloud data warehouse, and with dbt.
  • Business Partnership: Experience defining business metrics with Finance or business stakeholders, and reconciling data to financial systems.
  • Software Mindset: Experience with GitHub for version control and code review, automated builds (GitHub Actions or similar), and Jira and Confluence for work tracking and documentation.
  • Communication: Strong communication with people who aren't data specialists, and ability to execute under minimal supervision.
  • Growth Mindset: Motivated to learn new technologies and develop new skills.
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in computer science, statistics, economics, information systems, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Semantic Layer: Experience with a semantic layer, such as Snowflake semantic views or the dbt Semantic Layer, preferred.
  • Domain Knowledge: Experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, or Stripe data, and with subscription revenue, retention, or payments metrics, preferred.
  • Forecasting & ML: Experience preparing data for forecasting or machine learning models preferred.
  • Healthcare: Healthcare or HIPAA experience preferred.
  • Additional Tools: Familiarity with Tableau, Terraform, or Okta a plus.
  • Certifications: dbt Analytics Engineering or SnowPro certifications preferred.

title: Software Engineer AI Coding Tasks
description:
We're looking for experienced software engineers to build AI coding tasks from a codebase they know well. US$400-US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.

You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.

Remote, any location. US$400-US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.

How it works

  1. Apply. Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.

  2. Propose. Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.

  3. Build. In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.

  4. Stress-test. Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.

  5. Model testing. Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.

  6. Review. A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.

  7. Next task. Once your task is accepted, start another.


Requirements

  • 2+ years of professional software engineering

  • Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)

  • Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++

  • Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing

  • Regular use of an AI coding tool

  • Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models

  • You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words

  • At least 10 hours a week, starting now

  • A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)


Nice to have

  • Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure

  • Experience building agent tasks or RL environments


Terms

  • Between US$400 - US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you

  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms

  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us

  • Don't publish the work anywhere: no public pull request or public fork


Apply at https://www.askable.com/experts/roles/senior-software-engineer

title: Research Engineer Privacy and Anonymization
description:
Location: San Francisco or Singapore (on-site), or remote (Singapore or US Pacific time zones)
Start Date: ASAP
Languages: English
Team: Engineering

About the Role

Our client is a fast-growing AI company building reliable, fair and open infrastructure for AI training data. Their marketplace helps the people who create data get value for it, and gives AI labs trustworthy data to train on. It is already used by startups, Fortune 500 companies and frontier labs, and the company is backed by leading venture investors, including Y Combinator. They are scaling quickly to meet strong demand.

We are looking for a Research Engineer, Privacy and Anonymization to build the systems that make sensitive, real-world data safe and still useful for AI training. You will develop methods to detect and remove personally identifiable information, secrets and other sensitive content from raw data before it enters processing and synthetic data pipelines â protecting privacy without destroying the structure and signal that make the data valuable for training agents.

This is a privacy and data-protection engineering seat, not a synthetic-task design role. You will own the pipeline that stands in front of downstream processing, training, evaluation and synthetic generation.

This is a full-time role, starting ASAP. Offices are in San Francisco and Singapore; remote candidates are welcome if their working hours can overlap about 70â80% with either San Francisco (US Pacific) or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring.

What You'll Do

  • Build systems to detect PII, quasi-identifiers, credentials and other sensitive information, and design transformations based on the data type and the downstream use case.

  • Develop and benchmark detection approaches that combine rules, statistical models, classifiers and LLM-based methods.

  • Build production pipelines that anonymize raw data before it enters downstream processing, training, evaluation or synthetic data generation.

  • Create evaluation frameworks that measure privacy risk and retained data utility, including recall-weighted metrics, leakage tests and adversarial re-identification attempts.

  • Design systems that stay robust to new data sources, schema drift, unusual formats and sensitive information embedded in unexpected fields.

  • Work with engineering, research, operations and customers to translate privacy requirements into practical technical policies and safeguards.

What We're Looking For

  • Strong proficiency in Python, and experience building reliable production data or machine-learning systems.

  • Experience with information extraction, named-entity recognition, classification, or related methods for detecting rare or sensitive content.

  • Strong experimental instincts, and the ability to compare approaches across recall, precision, latency, cost and downstream data utility.

  • An understanding of the difference between redaction, masking, pseudonymization, anonymization and synthetic data â and when each is appropriate.

  • High attention to detail, and the ability to reason about subtle leakage paths, edge cases and adversarial failure modes.

  • Experience building data-processing pipelines end to end, including where there was no fully prescribed roadmap.

  • Clear written and spoken English, and comfort collaborating across teams and time zones.

  • Strong candidates may also have hands-on experience with privacy-enhancing technologies (such as differential privacy, k-anonymity, secure aggregation or format-preserving encryption); have worked with sensitive data in healthcare, finance or security; have built low-latency or high-throughput ML inference or data-processing systems; or have taken work from early research through to production.

  • Technical aptitude and learning potential matter more than years of experience. Motivated candidates are encouraged to apply even if they don't meet every point above.

Why This Role Matters for You

  • Make real-world data safe to train on: You will build the systems that let sensitive data be used for AI training without exposing people or secrets.

  • Privacy without wrecking utility: The job is not only to redact, but to keep the structure and signal that downstream training and synthetic pipelines need.

  • From detection to production: You will own the full path: detection methods, transformations, evaluation, and the pipeline that sits in front of training and generation.

  • Hard, high-stakes edge cases: Work on leakage paths, schema drift and adversarial failure modes, not only clean benchmark datasets.

  • San Francisco, Singapore, or remote: Work on-site in San Francisco or Singapore, or remotely, with hours that overlap about 70â80% with either US Pacific or Singapore business hours. The exact daily schedule will be agreed during hiring.

A workflow is a visual sequence of steps, covering inputs, generation, brand assets, scoring, branching logic and delivery, that a person builds once and runs again whenever the job repeats, on demand or on a schedule. This role owns that product and the connections that feed it, with one goal: more workflows built and run, by more people, across every customer.

You will own Workflows and Integrations. That covers the workflow builder, templates, scheduling and run management, and the steps that workflows are built from. It also covers the platform's third-party connections outside media: digital asset management systems, file storage such as Google Drive, translation services, data services such as Foreplay, and more than a hundred other business tools. You will make those connections part of the workflow itself, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them. You will build them on a common framework, so that each new connection is quicker to ship than the last and client teams can build on it for individual clients.

You will also own how workflows show up inside Scribble, our creative agent. Agents can already run as steps inside a workflow. The next step is for Scribble to find, build, change and run workflows on a person's behalf and report back as they run, and for a workflow to pause for a person's decision and act on it. You will work closely with the team that builds Scribble, and you will own the workflow experience it works through, so that a workflow behaves the same whether a person or an agent is driving it. When that works, building a workflow stops being a specialist job.

Key responsibilities

  • Own the charter for Workflows and Integrations: the durable problem, success metrics, and an explicit in and out scope list.

  • Grow adoption across every customer, measured by the number of workflows built and run and the number of people building them.

  • Make building a workflow simple enough for a marketer or creative to do without help, through templates, guided set-up and defaults that cover the common jobs.

  • Own the workflow experience that Scribble works through, so that an agent can find, build, change and run a workflow with the same tools a person uses.

  • Make human review part of the run: a workflow should pause for a person's decision, record it, and continue down the right path.

  • Make runs dependable at volume, with scheduling, run management, failure handling and clear status, so that a team trusts a workflow to run unattended.

  • Own third-party integrations outside media, from digital asset management and file storage to translation and data services, and make them built-in steps in a workflow, so that a run can start from a client's systems and deliver back into them.

  • Set the integration framework and standards that client teams build on when they connect a system for a single client.

  • Work with customers to find the jobs they repeat every week and turn them into workflows and templates that others can reuse.

  • Run the full lifecycle from discovery to post-launch review, with a written hypothesis before every ship and a review against it afterwards.

  • Use product data and structured customer feedback to set priorities, working backwards from evidenced customer need.

  • Partner closely with design on the builder experience, and with engineering on run reliability and the integration framework. Partner with the PMs who own Scribble, agents and the editor, and with the client teams who build on your framework.

Your background

You will have three to five years of product management experience, and you want to own a key product and take it to the next level. You might be a great fit if you can walk us through:

  • A product you grew from a small group of power users to broad adoption, and what you changed to get there.

  • Shipping a builder, automation or workflow tool, and what you learned about making something powerful easy to start with.

  • Building integrations with third-party platforms or APIs: how you chose which to build, and how you kept them working.

  • A time you built from validated customer need in a domain you had to go and learn. If your instinct is to start with a demo, this is not the role.

  • A decision you changed because the data told you to. Fluent in qual and quant.

  • Experience with AI agents or AI-assisted products is a plus.

You'll Thrive Here If Youâ¦

  • Move Fast. You're comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, iterating quickly, and fixing things before they become fires;

  • Stay Human. You care deeply about users and teammates, and design with empathy for real workflows;

  • Act Like an Owner. You take responsibility for outcomes, not just outputs. You spot problems early and take initiative to fix them.

  • Keep It Simple. You fight unnecessary complexity, design reusable patterns, and make hard things feel intuitive.

  • Love to Surprise. You enjoy finding unexpected ways to delight users, especially in the last mile of polish and usability.

KPIs & Success Measures

We will measure success through outcomes and quality, not just output:

  • Builder share (lead): percentage of monthly active users who build or edit a workflow. Target [TBD]%.

  • Workflow adoption (lead): percentage of monthly active users who run a workflow. Target [TBD]%.

  • Workflow run growth: month-on-month percentage growth in workflow runs. Target [TBD]%.

  • First workflow conversion: percentage of new users who complete a successful run within their first [TBD] days.

  • Share of generations through workflows: percentage of all generations produced by workflow runs.

  • Agent and human collaboration: percentage of workflow runs built or started by Scribble.

  • Connector adoption: percentage of active workspaces that use at least one third-party connection in a workflow each month. Target [TBD]%.

  • Integration usage: percentage of workflow runs that start from, or deliver to, a third-party connection. Target [TBD]%.

  • Reliability (hygiene bar): percentage of runs that complete without manual intervention, held at or above [TBD]%.

  • Learning velocity (supporting): percentage of launches reviewed after release against their stated hypothesis. Target 100%.

Benefits

  • 25 days PTO plus public holidays, although we operate a Flexible Time Off scheme

  • Health insurance / private medical cover

  • Monthly stipend towards wellness, fitness, and learning and development

  • Remote - work from anywhere in your home country

  • Enhanced parental leave policies, whether you become a parent through birth, adoption or surrogacy

  • Access to our Pencil office in The Shard, London for our UK employees

  • Flexible working hours

Deep Dive About Pencil

Pencil uses AI to make ads. Our mission is to make marketing effective and effortless. We want to become the default way ads get made - because AI ads are 10x faster and cheaper to make, and 2x better performing, than making them without AI.

We're called Pencil because we believe AI will be a tool for creative people, not a replacement - it may even be as fundamental a tool in the future as the pencil was in the past.

Pencil was founded in 2018 with a team from Google, Facebook and Uber with backing from Sequoia and Entrepreneur First. We were acquired by The Brandtech Group in 2023 to pursue a shared vision of bringing GenAI to the Fortune 500.

https://www.trypencil.com

About The Brandtech Group

The Brandtech Group's mission is to be the best company in the world at helping leading global brands drive growth by connecting content, data and media using technology.

It was founded in June 2015 (as You & Mr Jones) by former Havas Global CEO David Jones, with a simple mission to help brands do their marketing better, faster and cheaper using technology. It was renamed The Brandtech Group in January 2022.

Today it generates more than $1BN in revenue and is the largest global digital content partner for many of the world's biggest brands and companies, often using its unique in-housing model. It works with eight of the world's top 10 global advertisers and 49 of the world's top 100. Clients include Banco ItaÃº, Danone, Google, Intuit, LVMH, Microsoft, Morgan-Stanley, Netflix, Reckitt, Renault-Nissan, PayPal, TikTok, Uber and Unilever.

In addition, the Group invests in cutting-edge technology companies relevant to and with potential in marketing and has been investing in the AI, AR and the metaverse space since 2015. The Group was the first external investor in Niantic (creators of PokÃ©mon Go), alongside investments in AI Foundation (AI digital twins, personalized AI, and deep-fake detection 2018), Automat (AI chatbots, 2016), Elsy (AI media planning, 2016), Jivox (dynamic automated content, 2016), Crossing Minds (deep learning AI recommendation system, 2017), CreativeX (AI-driven content optimization, 2022), Zappar (AR, 2017), Provenance (blockchain, 2022) and GGP (the world's largest gaming fund).

CivilGrid is the trusted civil design platform powering affordable infrastructure renewal and growth. We give utilities, civil engineers, and municipalities a single, collaborative source of truth for what's underground so teams can plan, design, and build faster, smarter, and safer.

We're a venture-backed Series A startup tackling a $4.7T US infrastructure market that has been underserved by software for decades. Founded by industry insiders, each with 10+ years in utilities and civil engineering, we move fast, ship work that matters, and stay close to the customers and field teams we build for.

About Claims

AI ate the Internet, but it can't digest science yet. A paper is thousands of words of prose written for humans, but an AI agent doing research needs to know what was claimed, what evidence supports it, and how far to trust it. Claims turns the scientific literature into exactly that: every claim, tied to its evidence, as structured data that models and agents can query.

We're a startup and run as Subnet 111 on Bittensor. Since our mainnet launch on 28 August 2026, an open competition of miners has processed more than 10,000 papers, and every record was checked by our validator before it entered the dataset. The competition keeps raising the bar: miners keep finding ways to beat our own reference pipeline, and every win becomes part of the standard the whole network is scored against.

The team

Claims was founded by two professors of economics and a senior engineer.

  • Philipp Koellinger, CEO, is a professor of economics and an experienced entrepreneur: founder of DeSci Labs and the DeSci Foundation, and co-builder of SciWeave with Ogban.
  • Christian Roessler, co-founder, is a professor of economics and game theorist. He designs the incentive mechanism that makes the miner competition work.
  • Ogban Ugot, engineering, is a senior backend and machine learning engineer. He built SciWeave, the Claims miner, validator and data pipeline, and you will work with him every day.

You would be the fourth person on the team and our second engineer.

Our culture

We are a fully remote team spread across Europe, Africa and the US West Coast. We have a flat hierarchy and move fast towards clearly defined goals. We think deep, don't shy away from difficult problems or conversations, and we ship relentlessly. The code you will write will run on a live network within your first weeks, and you own real things from day one. We are an AI-native company and expect you to be an AI-native Software Engineer we can trust.

About the role

Position: Software Engineer (Python, full-stack)
Location: Remote. You need to be able to join our team meetings in the afternoon, Central European Time.
Type: Full-time contractor. Start in December 2026 or January 2027.

We're looking for a Software Engineer to help maintain and build Claims and its supporting applications, services, and developer tools. Claims turns scientific research into structured claims and supporting evidence through document processing, AI pipelines, and automated evaluation.

This is a hands-on, backend-focused full-stack role. You'll work across Python services, web dashboards, data pipelines, integrations, and deployment tooling. Your work will combine delivering new features with debugging existing systems, improving reliability, and making the codebase easier to maintain.

You should be comfortable owning well-defined tasks from investigation through implementation, testing, and release, working with the team on larger design decisions and unfamiliar areas.

Responsibilities

  • Build and maintain Python backend services, APIs, command-line tools, and background processing workflows.
  • Develop and improve web dashboards and internal review tools using TypeScript, React, and modern web frameworks.
  • Maintain pipelines that ingest research papers, process documents, extract structured information, and evaluate results.
  • Integrate external APIs and AI model providers, handling validation, retries, timeouts, rate limits, and usage costs.
  • Work with relational databases and object storage, including schema changes, migrations, queries, and data integrity checks.
  • Investigate bugs and production issues across services, pipelines, and interfaces; address root causes and add useful regression coverage.
  • Help maintain deployment automation, continuous integration, logging, monitoring, and operational documentation.
  • Improve existing code through practical refactoring, dependency maintenance, automated tests, and code review.
  • Collaborate with engineering and research colleagues to turn requirements and experimental workflows into reliable software.

Required skills and experience

  • Typically 1â5 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent practical experience delivering and maintaining production software.
  • Strong Python skills, including building maintainable services or data processing applications, managing dependencies, and writing automated tests.
  • Experience designing, consuming, and troubleshooting HTTP APIs, with a sound understanding of JSON, validation, authentication, and error handling.
  • Working knowledge of TypeScript or JavaScript and experience contributing to React applications or a comparable modern frontend framework.
  • Practical SQL and relational database experience, including data modelling, migrations, and debugging queries.
  • Confidence working in Linux environments and using the command line to investigate logs, configuration, processes, and service failures.
  • Experience with Git, pull requests, code review, automated testing, and continuous integration.
  • An understanding of secure engineering practices, including access controls, secrets management, and careful handling of private data.
  • The ability to navigate an existing codebase, trace issues across components, and make focused, well-tested changes.
  • Clear communication, practical problem-solving, and the judgment to work independently while asking for input when requirements or risks are unclear.

Nice to have

  • Experience with FastAPI, Pydantic, PostgreSQL, Supabase, Next.js, or similar tools.
  • Experience integrating LLM APIs, building AI-assisted workflows, or evaluating model outputs for accuracy, reliability, latency, and cost.
  • Familiarity with PDF parsing, OCR, document extraction, scientific datasets, or evidence provenance.
  • Experience with distributed jobs, asynchronous processing, reproducible pipelines, or automated benchmarking.
  • Familiarity with Docker, Ansible, systemd, GitHub Actions, cloud hosting, or infrastructure automation.
  • Experience with Bittensor, decentralized compute networks, or systems for evaluating independently submitted code.
  • Exposure to Rust, native Python extensions, or WebAssembly.
  • An interest in scientific research, open-source software, and tools that make research easier to inspect and reuse.

You don't need experience with every technology listed. Strong engineering fundamentals and the ability to learn quickly across the stack matter most.

What success looks like

  • You can independently deliver scoped features and fixes across the backend and supporting web applications.
  • Your changes are understandable, tested, and documented, with appropriate attention to security and compatibility.
  • You help make processing pipelines and production services more reliable and easier to troubleshoot.
  • You contribute constructively to reviews, communicate progress and blockers, and help the team turn research ideas into maintainable software.

What we offer

  • $1500 - $2000 per month, depending on experience.
  • Opportunities for rapid professional growth in a high-impact role: a small team, a live network, and a senior engineer to learn from.
  • Quarterly team retreats in inspiring locations (e.g., Vilnius, Koh Samui).
  • Travel and visa support for business needs.
  • Flexible remote working.


Help us build the data layer that lets AI do science properly.

How to apply


Apply online through the link here: https://airtable.com/appZKkV7FT7eYBhKI/shrjJ3jYfxZjsNckR

It takes about 30 minutes: a few practical questions, four short written answers, links to your code, and your CV or personal website. No cover letter needed.

We read every application after the deadline and reply to everyone.

title: Software Engineer Infrastructure
description:
Software Engineer, Infrastructure

Hybrid in Palo Alto (Mon / Wed / Thurs) Â· $185Kâ$215K base + meaningful early-stage equity + full benefits

Â 

About Sodalis

Specialty pharmacy is where the most complex and expensive drugs reach the most in-need patients, and it still runs on faxes, phone tag, and manual data entry. Patients wait weeks for therapies that can't wait.

Sodalis is building AI agents that run those operations end to end: reading and validating prescriptions, handling phone calls, and moving prescriptions through eligibility and fulfillment. The ambition goes beyond that. We want to be the rails every specialty prescription runs on, and the first system to perform clinical review at the standard of a pharmacist.

We're already in production, processing tens of thousands of prescriptions a week. Backed by Gradient Ventures (Google's AI fund), and founded by veterans of Apple's Applied ML, Included Health, and Avella Specialty Pharmacy (scaled to $1.5B+ before its acquisition by OptumRx).

Â 

The Opportunity

Everything we run today is cloud-based, and so are the pharmacy management systems we integrate with. But most of the specialty pharmacy market runs on-prem. To reach it, our system has to run on the pharmacy's systems instead of ours. Whether that's the full stack on-site or a hybrid split with our cloud is one of the first decisions you'd make. That's the problem you'd own.
We've never shipped an on-prem deployment, so there's no pattern to follow. You'll decide how our architecture gets packaged and deployed into environments we don't control, what has to change in our current infrastructure to make that possible, and how we maintain and see into those deployments once they're live.

We don't yet know what these environments look like in detail. Some pharmacies may have restricted outbound access, legacy hardware, or IT teams that can't give us a login; others may be more open. Part of the job is going in with our customer, finding out what's actually there, and designing something that works across the range.
You'll start with our AI pharmacy tech product, rolling out with a committed customer, so you build against a real deployment instead of a hypothetical one. You'd work directly with the founders and the early engineering team on the architecture.

What you'll do

  • Decide how our architecture runs in a pharmacy's environment, starting with the AI pharmacy tech product: full stack on-site, a hybrid split with our cloud, or something in between.

  • Adapt our current infrastructure and build the packaging and deployment path that installs and updates Sodalis at each pharmacy.

  • Own those deployments over time: upgrades, rollbacks, and observability into health and failures without being on site.

  • Go in with our customer and pharmacy IT teams to learn what their environments actually allow, and design for the range.

  • Partner with the founders and early engineering team on architecture.

What we're looking for

  • 5+ years in infrastructure or platform engineering.

  • You've taken an AWS-native stack and made it run on Kubernetes or similar in environments you don't operate, including stateful services.

  • You've shipped and maintained software running in environments you don't control: on-prem, customer-hosted, edge, or embedded.

  • You've kept a fleet of remote installs updated, observable, and recoverable without being able to log into them.

  • You've set the first pattern for something in a startup and are comfortable with ambiguity.

  • You'll spend time with pharmacy IT teams and need to understand their constraints firsthand. No healthcare background required.

How we work

We're a handful of people going all in on a problem we think is worth it, holding a high bar and shipping work that reaches real patients. It's intense, and it isn't for everyone. We want people who want to build something that matters, alongside others who care as much as they do. If that's you, we should talk.

title: Scientific Account Executive
description:
Adaptyv is building an automated lab that lets AI agents run biology experiments.

We're entering the era of agentic science where AI models can now design novel proteins, propose hypotheses, and iterate on experimental results. But they can't run the experiments themselves - that's still a manual, months-long process. We're building the infrastructure that gives AI agents access to the physical world.

We are one of the fastest growing biotech companies, trusted by leading biopharmas, frontier AI labs, and the techbio companies pushing the field forward. This is a rare chance to help advance some of the most important work happening in biotech today.

Our automated lab is powered by a deep software + hardware stack: lab instruments worth millions of USD reverse-engineered into API-controllable hardware, dozens of devices orchestrated through complex workflows, full observability on everything that happens in the lab, processing pipelines for messy physical-world data, and AI systems that troubleshoot production results and accelerate assay development.

Weâre growing rapidly and are hiring for talented people to scale and support the massive demand for AI-driven wet lab experimentation.

About the role

This is a hybrid sales and customer success role for someone with real scientific depth. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers â from first conversation through ongoing engagement. That means understanding what a protein design team is actually trying to achieve, helping them pick the right assays, making sure their experiments are set up correctly, and translating results back into language that's useful for their programs.

The day-to-day:

  • Running technical sales calls where you discuss binding kinetics, expression systems, and assay design, not just pricing

  • Onboarding new customers and helping them design their first experiments on the platform

  • Monitoring ongoing accounts, flagging issues early, and proactively suggesting next steps based on their results

  • Working with the biology team to troubleshoot when a customer's experiment doesn't go as expected

  • Identifying expansion opportunities within existing accounts â new targets, new assay types, larger campaigns

You won't be handed a script. You'll need to understand the science well enough to earn trust from PhD-level protein engineers and CSOs, while also being commercially sharp enough to close deals and grow accounts.

Responsibilities

  • Own the full customer lifecycle: prospecting, technical sales conversations, deal closing, onboarding, and ongoing account management.

  • Serve as the technical point of contact for customers. Understand their protein engineering goals and recommend the right experiments (binding, expression, thermostability, enzyme activity).

  • Understand and explain our assay capabilities in depth: BLI, SPR, cell-free expression, and emerging assay types. Know when each is appropriate and what the data means.

  • Work closely with the biology team to ensure experiments are designed correctly and results are communicated clearly.

  • Build and maintain a pipeline of commercial opportunities across customer segments: AI-driven protein design companies, biotech startups, pharma R&D teams, and academic labs.

  • Develop proposals and quotes tailored to customer needs, from small pilot experiments to large-scale data generation campaigns.

  • Represent Adaptyv at conferences and industry events. Be able to have deep technical conversations at the booth, not just hand out brochures.

  • Feed customer insights back to the product and biology teams: what assays are people asking for, what's missing, where are we losing deals.

What we're looking for

  • Scientific background in protein engineering, biochemistry, biophysics, or a related field. You should be comfortable discussing binding kinetics (KD, kon, koff), expression systems, and assay design without needing to look things up.

  • Experience in a customer-facing technical role: field application scientist, technical sales, scientific account management, or similar. CRO or biotech vendor experience is a strong plus.

  • Genuine interest in AI-driven protein design and the companies working in this space. You follow what's happening in the field.

  • Sell-Through & Brand Activation: Shift the focus from sell-in to sell-through. Partner with retail marketing and activation teams to execute high-impact programs, elevate in-store positioning and shelf execution, and consistently use retail assets to drive account performance.

What You'll Need to Succeed

Your application is always reviewed by a recruiter and all our hiring decisions are made by people. At Polaroid we believe two things can be true at once: technology can help us move forward, while human creativity, craft, judgement and real-world connection matter more than ever.

Since our beginning, we've embraced technology to create meaningful human experiences. Today that means exploring new tools, including AI, with curiosity and care, using them where they help us work better and build a stronger business, while staying true to what defines our brand.

title: Lead Systems Engineer (Orbital Launch)
description:
Lead Systems Engineer

We are looking for a Lead Systems Engineer to act as the Systems Technical Authority for our orbital rocket programme. You will lead the vehicle-level systems effort, maintaining a coherent technical view of the complete vehicle and leading the definition, management, and resolution of system interfaces.

Working with multidisciplinary teams across avionics, software, structures, propulsion, GNC, and more, you will manage the interdependencies between technical departments and use model-based systems engineering (MBSE) to keep system-level decisions connected. Your work will lay the technical foundation for successful vehicle integration and launch.

About us

We’re a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications.

We are already launching suborbital and ballistic rockets on a regular basis, generating significant revenue and applying our knowledge toward the development of an orbital rocket.

We are working hard to build something truly spectacular.

To thrive here you will need to be comfortable working at pace, with the autonomy to make decisions and execute on them quickly. If you’re excited by hard technical challenges and want a role where you will make a real difference each day to the future of the company, we may be the place for you.

At our company, job titles and career progression are earned, not determined by years of experience alone. They reflect the responsibility you take on and the dedication you bring to each project. If you’re ready to rise to the challenge, we’d love to hear from you.

Key responsibilities

  • Act as the Systems Technical Authority for the orbital rocket programme, providing vehicle-level systems leadership and maintaining technical coherence across the complete vehicle.

  • Lead the definition, ownership, and resolution of system interfaces across avionics, software, structures, propulsion, GNC, and other technical departments.

  • Identify and manage interdependencies, assumptions, constraints, and cross-subsystem impacts as the vehicle design develops.

  • Use MBSE models and related system artefacts to maintain a connected view of vehicle architecture, requirements, and interfaces.

  • Lead cross-disciplinary systems discussions and reviews, bringing forward system-level trade-offs, resolving technical conflicts, and ensuring decisions are clearly recorded.

  • Coordinate technical departments around vehicle-level priorities and help keep subsystem work aligned with the needs of the overall programme.

  • Track system-level issues and interface actions through to resolution, helping establish the conditions for successful vehicle integration and launch.

What we’re looking for

  • Strong understanding of model-based systems engineering and its application to complex, multidisciplinary engineering programmes.

  • Strong understanding of rocketry and how vehicle subsystems interact across the complete system.

  • Experience leading systems engineering work, system interfaces, or cross-disciplinary technical efforts on complex engineering projects.

  • A proven track record of successfully completing engineering projects.

  • The ability to maintain a vehicle-level perspective while engaging with technical teams across avionics, software, structures, propulsion, GNC, and other disciplines.

  • Confidence facilitating technical decisions, managing competing subsystem needs, and driving interface issues toward resolution.

Benefits and important information:

  • We offer top-decile compensation packages, bonuses and meaningful equity, to attract exceptional aerospace talent.

  • Every employee is awarded stock options in the company, you will directly benefit from your own hard work and success.

  • Comprehensive relocation support including flights, shipping and visas.

  • Lunch, dinner and drinks provided everyday

  • Free access to shared company housing

Please note, we are a fast paced, hyper-scaling startup. You will need to be comfortable working extended hours with high levels of autonomy, ownership, and flexibility, with contracts structured around a 48-hour working week.

We are committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace where everyone feels valued, has equal access to opportunity, and can thrive. We welcome different perspectives, backgrounds, and experiences—and believe our differences make us stronger.

Please submit applications in English

title: Engineering Intern
description:
About Atira

Atira builds the commercial brain for industrials. Our agents 10x the sales engineers of today by offering the complete toolbox of tasks needed in complex environments. They handle everything from extracting and classifying requirements from incoming RFQs, orchestrating communication and information retrieval across multiple stakeholders and systems, while generating outcomes like documentation, production system inputs, or configuration recommendations. CRM. Atira. ERP.

We are one of the fastest growing teams in Munich and are looking for you to join us!

Why engineers are the foundation of everything Atira ships

As an Engineering Intern at Atira, you will work on frontier AI technology, such as (recursive) agent harnesses, runtimes, evals, inference and self-verification in complex engineering domains. You build the frameworks, primitives and scaffolding that let agents reliably handle complex industrial processes end to end, from the first inbound RFQ to the write-back into ERP.

Misreading or wrongly interpreting a spec can cost a manufacturer six figures, so the challenges are real and the margin for error is thin.

Where you trained matters less than what you've built and how clearly you can describe what broke. Atira is at a stage where you must own problems end to end, because what you ship today is what our customers use tomorrow.

What you will do

  • Work on the agent runtime and harnesses. You improve the core components that let Atira's agents reason in complex engineering environments across the entire sales-engineering lifecycle, orchestrate themselves recursively at scale through dynamic programs, and handle arbitrarily large amounts of data. This includes the runtime/sandboxing, the harness, and the outer orchestration layer that ties it together

  • Build out our AI moat. You are in charge of improving quality & evals, improving the ontology layer that unlocks compounding process knowledge and fusing deterministic guardrails with agentic agency to make our agents actionable at enterprise level complexity

  • Unlock industrial scale. Industrials live in multi-modal, data-heavy environments: 1000-page inbounds, pricing lists, CAD files, ERP tables, legacy applications. You scale the AI systems behind them to millions of concurrent LLM requests in isolated sandboxes, with no silent failures, cost blowouts or latency explosions.

  • Advance our internal tooling. FDEs, platform engineers and the GTM team depend on tooling you build to improve Atira's internal context layer, ambient agents, insight and observability engines

  • Work with FDEs when customer problems hit the platform. When an FDE hits a problem they should be able to pull you in. At a team of 20, the boundary between AI, platform and customer is thin, and you'll cross it regularly

What we are looking for

Ownership, depth, and the instinct to take problems personally, go deep until you understand the system, and own the outcome including the parts that broke.

Your profile

  • Agent fluency sits on top of real engineering fundamentals. Solid skills in Python, TypeScript, or a comparable language. We value someone that can still code without AI. Ideally paired with hands-on experience with agents, evals, harnesses, runtimes, sandboxing and tools

  • You've gone further than most with AI-assisted development. Whether it's Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or your own setup, you've invested seriously in building the skills, context, and workflows to get maximum leverage from coding agents. This isn't a nice-to-have. We think engineers who have mastered this are fundamentally more productive, and we hire accordingly

  • You reason clearly about technical tradeoffs. You don’t need to have run systems at scale yet, but you can think through how a design would hold up at thousands of requests per second and explain the pros and cons of different approaches. Every design has tradeoffs: no free lunch

  • You’ve demonstrated ownership and initiative. A side project you took further than anyone asked, a serious open-source contribution, a research project or a startup. We want evidence that you build without being told to and can explain what broke and why

  • You have a strong technical foundation. Enrolled or recently graduated in Computer Science, Information Systems, AI, or a related technical field from a strong technical university (cracked dropouts can qualify too though)

  • Full working proficiency in English. German is not required

  • You're ready for a real internship, not a side gig. You can commit to at least three months full-time, on-site in Munich

What you'll get

  • Real ownership: you'll be one of the early team members and shape both product and architecture as well as work closely with customers

  • Strong peers and mentorship: work with and learn from engineers who have shipped AI systems in industrial environments at scale, with the opportunity for mentorship along the way

  • Impactful work: your code is deployed all across Europe’s and US industrial backbone, affecting how complex products and services are sold and configured worldwide

  • Competitive salary and additional benefits

  • Most importantly: Collaborate & thrive in a high-performing but caring culture. We will own the industrial sales function but will do so with modesty and integrity

What success looks like at the end of the internship

  • You've shipped meaningful improvements to the agent runtime, our AI pipelines and related systems that are running in production across multiple customer deployments

  • You own one well-defined piece of our AI stack end to end (an eval suite, an internal tool, part of the context layer or the SDK), and the team trusts your judgment on how it should evolve

  • When something breaks in the part you own, you can trace it end to end, from agent behaviour back to the agent infrastructure layer, and fix it

  • You’ve made an improvement to our internal AI tooling that the team now uses day to day

  • The design decisions in your piece have held up under real load, and you can explain the tradeoffs you made and what you’d do differently

  • If these metrics are met, we'd take you full-time without thinking twice

title: Senior Program Manager
description:
About us

INCO is a leading social enterprise on a mission to shape a more inclusive and sustainable economy that creates opportunities for all. We have teams and programs in over 50 countries. Our work spans five complementary activities:

  1. INCO Academy: skilling programs for people facing barriers to employment, leading to careers in fast-growing industries such as technology, sustainability and healthcare (400,000+ job seekers trained to date).

  2. INCO Kids: education and awareness programs giving school-age learners future-proof knowledge in technology, sustainability, citizenship and more (350,000+ learners supported to date).

  3. INCO Entrepreneurs: incubation and acceleration for underrepresented founders and social entrepreneurs (2,000+ businesses supported every year).

  4. INCO Ventures: impact investing and funding for social and environmental impact startups (€500M+ assets under management).

  5. INCO Spaces: co-working and co-living spaces for social and environmental innovators (Paris, Berlin, Warsaw and more).

About the program:

AI and the Future of Work is a new three-year research and policy-engagement program (2026–2029), funded through a research grant partnership and led end to end by INCO. It tracks AI's real-world impact on jobs, tasks and productivity across all 27 EU member states, and gives policymakers the evidence, trend baselines and scenario-planning tools to capture AI's productivity upside while managing the workforce transition.

About the role:

We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to run the AI and the Future of Work program day to day and make sure it delivers on time, on budget and to the grant's commitments. You will closely lead and collaborate with a Research Lead and a Policy Lead. 

You will turn a three-year grant into a working operation: a deliverables calendar across 27 countries, a consortium of up to 15 partners, a publication schedule and a reporting cycle the funder can trust. You need to be comfortable working alongside researchers and policy specialists, and fluent in the rhythm of grant-funded research programs.

Responsibilities:

Lead program delivery end to end 

Planning and implementation

  • Build and own the three-year implementation plan: workstreams, milestones, dependencies and the deliverables calendar agreed with the funder.

  • Run the program's operating rhythm: weekly core-team check-ins, monthly consortium updates and quarterly steering reviews.

  • Coordinate the publication pipeline with the Research and Policy Leads: quarterly data refreshes, five semi-annual reports, policy briefs, the annual flagship and the 2029 EU27 report.

  • Keep thorough program documentation: plans, decision logs, risk register and handover notes.

  • Set up quality-assurance steps for outputs (review cycles, sign-off, editorial and brand checks) together with the Communications team.

  • Run the semi-annual tracking cycle and the reporting calendar for the five P0 markets and five sub-regional clusters, so national and EU27 outputs land together.

Monitoring and evaluation

  • Define and track program KPIs and grant deliverables; spot slippage early and agree corrective action with the leads.

  • Collect and compile performance data across workstreams and partners, and report it to your manager and the funder in a structured, actionable way.

  • Coordinate the program's evaluation framework so the team can show what the evidence changed in policy and practice.

Budget and resources

  • Own the program budget and cost sheet, including consortium partner budgets and the research consolidation budget held by the Research Lead.

  • Manage timelines and scope so the program delivers within the grant's budget and rules; prepare budget forecasts and reallocation requests.

  • Ensure grant compliance: eligible costs, audit trail, data protection (GDPR) and the funder's reporting requirements, working with Finance and Legal.

Manage the consortium and partners 

  • Run the operational side of partner onboarding with the Research Lead: due diligence, contracts, scopes of work, payment schedules and data-sharing agreements.

  • Track the delivery of 8 to 15 national partners against their contracts, and manage underperformance or replacement when needed.

  • Organise consortium working groups, review cycles and annual convenings, and keep communication flowing across countries and time zones.

  • Run the secretariat for the sub-recipient advisory committee (INCO staff, funder representatives and independent experts): schedule meetings, prepare selection materials, record recommendations and keep the process transparent, with final selection resting with INCO.

  • Manage subrecipient compliance: flow-down of grant terms, financial and narrative reporting from partners, and checks before each payment.

Manage the funder and stakeholders

  • Act as the primary operational liaison with the grant funder, keeping expectations aligned and surfacing risks early.

  • Prepare and present progress, financial and impact reports to the funder and other key stakeholders.

  • Work with the Head of Partnerships on funder conversations, renewals and any extension of the partnership.

  • Support the Policy Lead and with the logistics of policymaker convenings, events and launches.

Coordinate the team

Diesen Datenschatz wollen wir noch konsequenter nutzen und die ganze Organisation befähigen, mit starkem AI-Enablement selbst mit Daten zu arbeiten. Dafür suchen wir dich. 

Du wirst Teil unseres Finance & BI Teams und arbeitest eng mit Controlling und BI. Wir bauen zusammen die Zahlenbasis, auf der Foodji gesteuert wird und gehen Fragen aus dem Business gemeinsam an: schnell, präzise und mit dem Anspruch, jede Frage bis zur Entscheidung durchzudenken.

Deine Mission bei Foodji

  • Ist-Zahlen & Treiber: Du analysierst gemeinsam mit dem Controlling die operativen Treiber hinter den Ist-Zahlen und leitest konkrete Maßnahmen ab für alle Teams.

  • Planung: Du baust treiberbasierte Modelle für Budget und rollierenden Forecast, inklusive Szenarien und Annahmen aus den Fachbereichen.

  • Reporting: Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit dem Controlling das Management-, Board- und Investorenreporting weiter, mit Fokus auf Treiber und Ausblick.

  • Business Cases & Unit Economics: Du bewertest neue Standorte, Kundensegmente, Pricing und Initiativen und findest die Hebel für Marge und Wachstum.

  • Metriken: Gemeinsam mit dem BI-Team definierst du Metriken und Business-Logik im Semantic Layer, damit alle mit denselben Zahlen arbeiten.

  • Business Partnering: Du bist Sparringspartner:in für Geschäftsführung, Sales, Account Management, Operations, Culinary und Marketing und begleitest die Umsetzung deiner Empfehlungen.

AI-native arbeiten

AI ist bei uns das Werkzeug, mit dem wir Analytics bauen. Wir arbeiten täglich mit AI-Tools wie Claude und Claude Code, direkt auf unserem Snowflake Data Warehouse.

  • Du nutzt AI, um Daten zu explorieren und zu analysieren sowie für die Automatisierung von wiederkehrenden Tasks.

  • Du prüfst Ergebnisse kritisch, auch die zugrunde liegenden Abfragen, bevor sie in eine Entscheidung gehen, und befähigst andere Teams, selbst mit Daten und AI zu arbeiten.

Das bringst du mit

  • 2 bis 5 Jahre Erfahrung in FP&A, Controlling, Corporate Finance, Beratung oder Investment Banking, idealerweise in einem schnell wachsenden Unternehmen.

  • Ein sehr gutes Studium in Wirtschaft, Finance, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Mathematik, Informatik oder einem verwandten Fach.

  • Sehr gute Modellierungsskills in Excel und Erfahrung mit BI-Tools wie Tableau.

  • Tempo und Ownership: Du wartest nicht auf Aufträge, siehst die nächste Frage, bevor sie gestellt wird, und bringst Dinge zu Ende.

  • Ein gutes Verständnis dafür, wie Zahlen, Operations und Go-to-Market zusammenhängen.

  • Du übersetzt komplexe Analysen in eine klare Botschaft, für das Management genauso wie für Kolleg:innen ohne Finance-Hintergrund und sprichst fließend Deutsch und Englisch.

  • Deutschkenntnisse auf muttersprachlichem Niveau sowie fließende Englischkenntnisse.

  • Ein Plus: Erfahrung in einem Startup oder Scale-up und ein Hintergrund in Food, Retail, Logistik oder einem anderen operativ geprägten Geschäftsmodell sowie Erfahrung mit einem Data Warehouse (z. B. Snowflake), SQL oder einem Semantic Layer.

DAS BIETEN WIR DIR

  • Echte Wirkung: Deine Analysen fließen direkt in Entscheidungen von Geschäftsführung und Fachbereichen.

  • Kurze Wege und enge Zusammenarbeit mit den Gründern.

  • Einen modernen Stack (Snowflake, Tableau, NetSuite, AI-Tools) und den Freiraum, ihn weiterzuentwickeln.

  • Ein Team, das gerade neu aufstellt, wie FP&A mit AI und Semantic Layer arbeitet, und dich dabei mitgestalten lässt.

NOCH FRAGEN?

Auch die Bereiche Unternehmen, Schulen und Tourismus möchten wir verstärkt ausbauen.

Daraus entstehen viele Geschichten und Möglichkeiten, neue Kunden zu erreichen. Dafür suchen wir jemanden, der bei uns im Team vor Ort arbeitet, Ideen einbringt und deren Umsetzung selbst in die Hand nimmt.

Du hast Dich bereits bei uns beworben?
Durch ein Versehen bei der Verwaltung sind uns leider einige Bewerbungen verloren gegangen. Wenn Du weiterhin Interesse an einer Zusammenarbeit hast, bewirb Dich bitte noch einmal bei uns. Entschuldige den zusätzlichen Aufwand!

Deine Aufgaben

  • Unsere Social-Media-Kanäle betreuen: Du planst Inhalte für Instagram, Facebook und TikTok, entwickelst einen Redaktionsplan und kümmerst Dich um Veröffentlichungen sowie Kommentare und Nachrichten.

  • Aus Aufnahmen fertigen Content machen: Du sichtest das Material aus unseren Projekten und schneidest daraus Reels, Stories und Werbevideos. Dazu gehören passende Einstiege, Untertitel und Texte. Grafiken setzt Du selbst um oder stimmst Dich mit unserem Grafikteam ab.

  • Mit Creatorn zusammenarbeiten: Wir bauen ein Netzwerk aus Creatorn in verschiedenen Regionen Deutschlands auf. Du briefst sie für ihre Einsätze, koordinierst Termine und sorgst dafür, dass sie die Aufnahmen liefern, die wir für unsere Inhalte und Kampagnen benötigen.

  • Bezahlte Kampagnen betreuen: Du setzt Anzeigen auf Instagram und Facebook auf, steuerst das vereinbarte Budget und entwickelst die Kampagnen weiter. Ziel ist, passende Interessenten zu erreichen und konkrete Anfragen/Leads für unsere Sammelprojekte zu gewinnen.

  • Werbemittel testen und verbessern: Du probierst unterschiedliche Videos, Grafiken und Anzeigentexte aus und prüfst, welche Varianten bei unseren Zielgruppen funktionieren.

  • Ergebnisse auswerten: Du behältst Reichweite und Interaktionen ebenso im Blick wie die Kosten und Qualität gewonnener Anfragen. Mit unserem Vertrieb besprichst Du, welche Kontakte zu passenden Projekten führen, und leitest daraus Verbesserungen ab.

Was du mitbringst

Du hast bereits Social-Media-Kanäle betreut und selbst Inhalte umgesetzt. Außerdem hast Du praktische Erfahrung mit bezahlter Werbung im Meta-Werbeanzeigenmanager. Du kannst uns an einem Beispiel erklären, welches Ziel Du verfolgt hast, was Dein eigener Anteil war und was Du aus den Ergebnissen gelernt hast.

Außerdem wünschen wir uns:

  • Einen sicheren Umgang mit einem Videoschnittprogramm wie CapCut, Premiere Pro oder DaVinci Resolve.

  • Ein Gespür für Gestaltung und verständliche Texte sowie Erfahrung mit einem Grafiktool wie Photoshop oder Canva.

  • Ein Verständnis dafür, wie man Kampagnenergebnisse bewertet und das eingesetzte Budget sinnvoll verteilt.

  • Eine organisierte Arbeitsweise: Du hältst Absprachen ein, setzt Prioritäten und behältst auch mehrere laufende Projekte im Blick.

  • Freude an der Zusammenarbeit mit Creatorn, unserem Team und den Menschen in unseren Partnervereinen.

  • Interesse daran, KI-Tools für Ideen, Content-Produktion und wiederkehrende Aufgaben sinnvoll einzusetzen.

Erfahrung mit Google Ads, Conversion-Tracking oder der Optimierung von Landingpages ist ein Plus. Du musst nicht jedes Tool bereits beherrschen. Für Social Media und Meta Ads solltest Du aber praktische Erfahrung mitbringen.

Eine bestimmte Ausbildung oder ein Studium setzen wir nicht voraus. Uns interessieren Deine Fähigkeiten und Deine bisherigen Arbeiten. Wenn Du selbst gerne vor der Kamera stehst, kannst Du Dich auch dort einbringen. Voraussetzung ist das nicht.

So arbeitest Du bei uns

Dein Arbeitsplatz ist bei uns im Büro in Gräfelfing bei München. Wir möchten den Bereich intern aufbauen und suchen jemanden, der im Arbeitsalltag vor Ort mit unserem Team zusammenarbeitet.

Du stimmst Dich direkt mit Geschäftsführung, Grafik, Projektmanagement und Vertrieb ab. Gemeinsam legen wir Ziele, Budgets und Prioritäten fest. Innerhalb dieses Rahmens organisierst Du Deine Aufgaben eigenständig.

Für Aufnahmen bei unseren Partnervereinen bauen wir parallel das Creator-Netzwerk auf. Bei Dir laufen die Inhalte zusammen, damit daraus ein verlässlicher Auftritt und wirksame Kampagnen werden.

Was Dich erwartet

  • Verantwortung und Gestaltungsspielraum: Du kannst unsere Kanäle und Abläufe von Anfang an mitentwickeln und eigene Ideen ausprobieren.

  • Projekte mit Geschichten: Vom ersten eigenen Sticker einer Jugendmannschaft bis zum Sammelalbum eines Profivereins gibt es viel zu erzählen.

  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit: Du arbeitest in einem kleinen Team mit kurzen Abstimmungswegen.

  • Ausstattung für Deine Arbeit: Die benötigte Hard- und Software stimmen wir passend zu Deinen Aufgaben ab.

  • Gemeinsame Erlebnisse: Ob Stadionbesuch oder Wiesn, auch außerhalb unserer Projekte unternehmen wir etwas zusammen. Kostenlose Getränke und Kaffee gehören im Büro dazu.

Zeig uns, was Du schon umgesetzt hast

Schick uns Deinen Lebenslauf oder einen kurzen Überblick über Deinen bisherigen Weg sowie passende Arbeitsproben. Das können betreute Kanäle, Videos, Grafiken oder Beispiele aus Werbekampagnen sein.

Schreib bei gemeinsamen Projekten bitte dazu, welche Aufgaben Du selbst übernommen hast. Bei Kampagnen interessieren uns das Ziel, Dein Vorgehen und die Ergebnisse. Das kannst Du auch anonymisiert darstellen.

Sag uns außerdem, wann Du starten könntest, welchen Stundenumfang Du suchst und welche Gehaltsvorstellung Du hast.

Bewirb Dich direkt hier über die Plattform. Wir freuen uns darauf, Dich und Deine Arbeiten kennenzulernen!

title: IT Systems Automation Engineer (f/m/x)
description:
bonial helps you save time, money and paper!

We are a digital advertising partner for offline businesses - we support retailers in their marketing activities and help them find a new audience. Would you like to join and be a part of digitalisation of retail?

bonial is part of Axel Springer SE and is disrupting the retail landscape as the leading "Drive to Store" partner in Germany and France. Through our platforms "kaufDA" and "MeinProspekt" in Germany, and “Bonial” in France, we connect millions of users with their favorite shops and brands—driving real impact every single day.
We are in the midst of an exciting growth phase, scaling fast and transforming the way people discover retail. At bonial, we thrive in a high-performance, fast-paced environment fueled by motivated, results-driven individuals who are passionate about making a difference. If you’re looking to be part of a dynamic team that’s shaping the future of retail, we’d love to meet you.


bonial welcomes both full- and part-timers!

About The Role

IT Operations keeps the company's core productivity, identity, and device ecosystem running smoothly and securely. As IT Systems Automation Engineer, you will own the design, implementation, and maintenance of automation across our corporate IT platforms (including M365, Google Workspace, JAMF, Microsoft Intune, Atlassian & Slack). You'll reduce manual work for the team, improve consistency and security across the employee lifecycle. You’ll help build the scripts, integrations, and workflows that let a 6-person team support the whole organization efficiently. This is a hands-on engineering role within IT Operations, not a helpdesk position - you'll spend most of your time building and improving systems rather than handling day-to-day tickets.

What You’ll Do

  • Automate the employee lifecycle: Design and maintain automated workflows for onboarding, offboarding, and role changes across M365, Google Workspace, JAMF, Intune, and Slack (provisioning/deprovisioning accounts, licenses, group memberships, and device enrollment)

  • Device management: Build and maintain JAMF (macOS/iOS) and Intune (Windows/mobile) configuration profiles, compliance policies, and automated patch/update workflows.

  • Identity & access automation: Automate group and license assignment, conditional access rules, and access reviews across M365 and Google Workspace, working closely with the security team where relevant.

  • Collaboration tooling: Manage and automate Slack workspace administration - channel provisioning, app/integration approvals, user lifecycle, and usage policies.

  • Scripting & integration: Write and maintain scripts (PowerShell, Google Apps Script, or similar) and use APIs to connect systems that don't natively integrate.

  • Documentation & runbooks: Document automation logic, workflows, and recovery procedures so the rest of the team can support and extend what you build.

  • Monitoring & reliability: Set up monitoring/alerting for automated workflows so failures (e.g., a broken onboarding script) are caught and resolved quickly.

  • Continuous improvement: Identify manual, repetitive IT Operations tasks and propose/build automation to eliminate them.

  • Vendor & tooling evaluation: Assess new automation tools or platform features (e.g., new Intune or JAMF capabilities) and recommend adoption where it adds value.

  • Agentic support: Design, build, and operate AI agents that resolve common IT support requests end-to-end (e.g., password resets, access and software requests, device troubleshooting) via Slack or the service desk, connecting them to M365, Google Workspace, JAMF, and Intune through APIs, with clear guardrails, approval steps, human escalation paths, and audit logging.

  • AI enablement: Roll out and administer AI tools across the organization (e.g., Microsoft Copilot, Claude AI/Code, or similar), including license assignment, data access and governance settings, and usage policies, working closely with security, legal, and the works council where relevant, and support employees with onboarding guides, training materials, and best practices.



What We’re Looking For

  • Required:

    • Experience in IT Operations, Systems Administration, or a similar role with hands-on scripting/automation responsibility.

    • Practical experience administering at least two of: Microsoft 365 (Entra ID/Exchange/SharePoint admin), Google Workspace, JAMF, Microsoft Intune.

    • Working proficiency in at least one scripting/automation language (PowerShell, Python, Bash, or Google Apps Script) and comfort using REST APIs.

    • Understanding of core identity and device management concepts: SSO, MDM/UEM, conditional access, device compliance.

    • Ability to document processes clearly for a small team that needs to maintain what you build.

  • Nice to Have:

    • Experience with Slack administration or Slack API/workflow automation.

    • Experience with a scripting/orchestration platform (e.g., Workato, Tines, Zapier, Azure Automation, or similar iPaaS tools).

    • Relevant certifications (e.g., Microsoft MS-102/MD-102, Jamf Certified Admin, Google Workspace Administrator).

    • Familiarity with security/compliance frameworks relevant to endpoint and identity management (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001).

    • Experience working on a small IT team where you own end-to-end delivery rather than a narrow slice of a larger org.

What We Offer:

High growth story - bonial is a high-growth and dynamic company with continuous potential into the future. We are a leading player and a driving force in an industry that is undergoing a massive and a once-in-a-lifetime shift from print to digital.

Innovation & tech - we are a high-tech company focused on innovative technology, leveraging AI and other tools to maximize productivity and efficiency. We leverage these tools to continually enhance the performance of our company and our people, while driving results for our customers and users.

Exciting environment for professional development - strong support for your professional development, backed-up by a feedback culture to help you identify your strengths and opportunities.

Diversity - proud to be an equal opportunity workplace where we aim to enable everyone to show up as their full selves. We are committed to equal employment opportunity and to being a safe space regardless of race, religion, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability, gender, gender identity or gender expression.

Wellbeing - we believe mental health is as important as being fit. That's why we're giving you free access to nilo.health, a mental health app. In terms of physical training, other than our awesome gym in the office, we also cover part of the subscription to the Urban Sports Club. We can also offer you a corporate pension scheme so you don't have to worry about your retirement.

Sustainability - together with our Green team, we offer you the opportunity to engage in projects that promote sustainability, environmental development and the impact that we make on our planet.

Flexibility - Currently, we have a policy that allows for up to 20% mobile work, which can be conducted from anywhere within Germany, and the option to work from abroad. Additionally, we offer 28 days of holiday. You also get an extra day for each calendar year (up to 30 days) as well as other occasions (moving, working on a social project, etc).*

Modern office - Zen Rooms where employees can pray, relax or simply have some quiet time; fully equipped gym in the office, and a roof terrace for amazing social events.

Free lunch – whenever you’re at the office, we offer you different lunch options – and it’s all on us! Enjoy your lunch at a nearby restaurant that partners with us! Hot and cold drinks, fruit, regular varied and healthy breakfasts and other snacks at the office are, of course, always available for free for our employees.*

Social Culture – which encourages people to start conversations, build relationships and participate together in the community through regular team events.

Partner for retail - we empower retailers to reach their customers in the most efficient and effective way possible. We see ourselves as a critical business partner for retail, and as highlighted in our Company Vision, we “Enrich local shopping for everyone. Everyday.”

As part of the Axel Springer Group, we also align with the Axel Springer Essentials.


If you think you could fit the bill, we'd love to hear from you!

You can check out our bonial_people Instagram or read more about bonial culture and tech on Medium.

*as per our current Works Agreements
